metadata.description: Post-core feature backlog for PhotoBlaze. These ship AFTER the core viewer is stable (roadmap Phases 0-3: window, decode-to-fit, prefetch ring, hold-to-fly). Every task obeys the prime directive (faster or perf-neutral) and the project's TDD rules: pure logic isolated and unit-tested, GPU work behind the Renderer seam, golden-image tests for visuals. Shared infrastructure is factored out so it is built once: a per-photo ViewTransform (rotation + zoom + scaling mode), a translucent HUD/overlay layer, and a central configurable action/keymap.

tasks.title: Windows: single-instance window reuse + Explorer multi-select as one playlist
tasks.description: Make Windows match the macOS open idiom (LaunchServices already gives the Mac one instance + one openURLs batch). Today each Explorer double-click/Open spawns a FULL new process (decode pool + resident VRAM ring each; settings.toml write races), and multi-select Open invokes one process per file (Explorer blocks >15 selections by default — MultipleInvokePromptMinimum — so the blast radius is capped at ~15 processes, but that is still bad). Plan: (a) accept multiple CLI path args -> classify_inputs (the Vec<PathBuf> -> LaunchInput::Files machinery already serves drag-drop/picker); (b) MultiSelectModel=Player on the ProgID (MSI AppRegistration component + the HKCU self-registration fallback in default_app.rs) so a multi-select arrives as ONE invocation; (c) single-instance: named mutex, loser forwards its paths via WM_COPYDATA to the running instance (-> open_paths -> open_plan) and exits, winner comes to front (AllowSetForegroundWindow) — this also merges the multiple invocations Explorer emits when a huge selection overflows the ~32K command line. Compare-two-photos is NOT this task: thats #43 (or a future explicit File > New Window command, which the mutex design must not preclude — e.g. a --new-window flag bypass). MSIX/Store evaluation moved out to decisions.md (revisit only if monetizing). Windows machine required.
tasks.details: Milestone C (ADR-018). Set-default: a button/hotkey opens ms-settings:defaultapps (or the Default Programs UI), since Windows forbids silent default seizure. Single-instance (optional): forward a newly-opened path to the running window (named pipe / mutex) instead of spawning a second window - nicer for double-click bursts; defer if it complicates the hot path. A modern Win11 inline folder verb would need an IExplorerCommand COM handler - only pursue if the 'Show more options' legacy verb from Task 13 feels inadequate. MSIX/Store: revisit only when charging money - it buys discovery + MS-managed signing/updates but costs the cheap folder verb and adds container friction.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual: 'Set as default' opens the right Settings page; a second launch with single-instance adopts the new photo in the existing window. MSIX evaluation deferred.

tasks.title: Clipboard affordances on the EXIF info panel (copy all / copy one field)
tasks.description: UNCOOKED IDEA (owner, 2026-06-28) - needs design before building. On the Shift+I full-EXIF overlay, add a small clipboard icon in the panel's corner that copies the whole info block as text, and let clicking an individual field copy just that one value. Could be genuinely useful for grabbing a camera/lens/exposure string or a file path without retyping. Capturing it as a low-priority backlog item, not a committed design.
tasks.details: EXPLORATORY - the interaction model is the open question, because the info/EXIF overlay is NOT egui. It's a software-composited RGBA8 pill rasterized in pb-app/src/hud.rs (render_table) and drawn as a single alpha-blended GPU quad via Renderer::set_overlay (one texture, rebuilt only on change, off the photo hot path). So unlike the Settings/About dialogs there are no interactive widgets to hang a click handler on - 'click a field to copy it' needs explicit HIT-TESTING: map the cursor position (minus the overlay's corner margin + the panel's row layout from render_table) back to a specific Row, then copy that row's value. That row geometry currently lives only inside the rasterizer, so it would need to expose per-row rects (or a click-to-row helper) for the event loop to test against. The whole-panel 'copy all' is the easy half: assemble the same Vec<Row> the panel renders (App::exif_rows) into text and write it. OPEN QUESTIONS to resolve first: (a) is text-on-an-overlay click-to-copy worth the hit-testing machinery, or should the full-EXIF view become a real interactive surface (egui) instead, which would make per-field copy/selection trivial but is a bigger change and pulls EXIF into the chrome stack; (b) discoverability + affordance - a static clipboard glyph in the corner implies 'copy all', but 'click any row to copy that row' is invisible without a hover highlight (which the static-bitmap overlay can't currently show without a rebuild per mouse-move); (c) feedback - reuse the existing toast ('Copied') so the user knows it worked. REUSE: clipboard text I/O can ride the same arboard dep added for image copy (#27, pb-app/src/clipboard.rs - currently set_image; add a set_text path); the corner icon would follow the HUD Font Awesome solid workflow (hud.rs icon compositing, FA solid per CLAUDE.md); exif_rows already builds the field list. Decide the interaction model (overlay hit-test vs. promote EXIF to egui) before committing to an implementation.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure: a unit test for 'rows -> clipboard text' (formatting, label:value lines, ordering) and, if the overlay hit-test route is taken, a pure cursor-position -> row-index mapping test (mirrors the render_table layout; off-panel / between-rows returns None). Manual: Shift+I, click the corner icon and paste the whole block elsewhere; click a single field and paste just that value; confirm the 'Copied' toast fires and that copying never writes anything to disk (privacy #2 - clipboard is a user-initiated action, not a viewing trace).

tasks.title: Flicker compare mode: pin (Shift+Y) + instant A/B toggle (Y)
tasks.description: Owner-approved 2026-07-03 — full design + implementation order in .taskmaster/docs/compare-mode-plan.md. Y pins the current photo, then flips instantly between the pin and wherever you are (full-screen flicker comparison — perceptually better than side-by-side for culling, and a keypress-is-a-rebind cheap in this engine). Shift+Y moves/clears the pin. Zoom/pan carries across same-dimension flips (the 100%-crop sharpness workflow). Pin is RAM-only (privacy ADR-018), survives playlist rebuilds by name, unpins on delete. The pinned texture is exempt from ring eviction so the flip never decodes. Split view demoted to an optional phase 2 reusing the same pin state; a future squoosh-style export preview can ride the same toggle seam. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-03: all five build subtasks landed in one session, workspace green (150+ tests incl. 7 new compare semantics tests + 2 playlist jump_to tests), clippy -D warnings, fmt, swift host builds. Live-smoked on the corpus: pin 1/15, browse, Y flips 1<->3 then 1<->4 (return point follows) — trace-verified.

tasks.title: AI image description (on-device / local models only)
tasks.description: DETAILED PLAN: .taskmaster/docs/ai-descriptions-plan.md (2026-07-03). Describe the current image with a vision model. Trigger: `D` (rebindable; menu + context menu), result overlaid where the detailed info panel goes; optional auto-describe when the user PARKS on an image >500 ms (EAGER_PREP_DELAY pattern) — cancelled on advance (generation counter), results cached RAM-only per image (meta_cache pattern), dropped on exit. Auto mode is an opt-in toggle: fine by construction on the Apple on-device backend, but a configured endpoint could be remote, and passive sends must be a deliberate choice. Two backends behind one core-owned seam/policy: (1) macOS 27+ Foundation Models framework (on-device, image input, ships with the OS); (2) an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (LM Studio / llama.cpp / Ollama — Qwen3-VL-8B or 27B-class on an RTX 5090) for Windows and power users. One-shot v1 (streaming later if slow; expected 1–5 s). Prompt built in core so both backends match: salient EXIF (capture time, camera/lens, raw GPS coords — offline reverse-geocoder is a LATER upgrade), filename + parent folder; all context framed as UNVERIFIED (trust-the-pixels instruction — hallucination guard) with epoch-default junk dates filtered out. Custom prompt template = advanced, settings.toml-only in v1 ({filename}/{folder}/{datetime}/{location}/{camera} placeholders). Optional TTS via CoreEffect::Speak — AVSpeechSynthesizer / Windows.Media.SpeechSynthesis, offline system voices, speech stops on navigation. New 'AI Descriptions' settings section (own tab on macOS): backend picker (Auto/Apple/Local), endpoint URL + model, auto-describe toggle, speak-aloud toggle. Privacy (ADR-018): never cloud, RAM-only, no sidecars/caches on disk; the endpoint URL + toggles are the only persisted config. v1 scope: on-disk stills (archive entries punted like Delete). Prerequisite: pb-hud font-fallback cascade — model output is arbitrary, possibly non-Latin prose. Additions from final discussion: 'Speak descriptions' is ALSO a menu toggle (Image menu, Mute-Live-Photo-Audio pattern, MenuState checkbox); the AI Descriptions settings section carries a short privacy blurb (custom endpoint = your images upload to that URL, incl. auto-describe — keep it local/trusted; online services may retain/train on images).

tasks.title: Copy Text from Image / Show Text (on-device OCR + QR codes)
tasks.description: DETAILED PLAN: .taskmaster/docs/ai-descriptions-plan.md (OCR section, 2026-07-03). Tier 1 only: on-demand OCR of the current image — 'Copy Text from Image' in the Edit/context menus (clipboard + toast) and `T` to show recognized text in a HUD panel. Engines are OS-built-in and fully on-device: macOS Vision RecognizeTextRequest (NO macOS 27 dependency — available on the current floor; Swift-side via the same delegate/FFI shape as the FM describe backend) and Windows.Media.Ocr via the windows crate (worker thread, downscaled input ≤ OcrEngine.MaxImageDimension, language packs required). Shares task #44's state machine (busy/generation-cancel/RAM-only cache) and the ClipboardPayload::Text seam. Tier 2 (VisionKit Live Text overlay) and Tier 3 (cross-platform selection UI) deliberately punted — recorded in the plan doc. GARNISH: QR/barcode payloads via a pure-Rust decoder (rxing or rqrr) on BOTH platforms (Windows has no OS barcode API; one shared backend, no FFI, testable with generated QR PNGs). ⚠ Decode from FULL-RES RGBA, not the OCR downscale (pixels-per-module). Payloads list above the text in the T panel and ride the copy command — no new key/menu item. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-04 (Windows + shared core; #44 not started, so the analysis state machine was built fresh in pb-app-core/image_text.rs for #44 to generalize later): Action::CopyImageText (id copy_text) + Action::ShowImageText (id show_text, default T); InfoMode::Text panel via new pb-hud render_paragraph (word-wrap block, first in the crate); TextScan worker (anim_decode shape: full-res decode + baked rotation -> rqrr QR on full-res gray -> Lanczos cap -> Windows.Media.Ocr via blocking IAsyncOperation::join(), first in tree — windows-future calls it join, not get); ClipboardPayload::Text grew an optional core-supplied toast (winit shell honors it; pb-mac-ffi clipboard_text_toast() accessor ready for Swift); archive entries WORK (pixel-based, no path needed). Deck-gen guard drops post-rebuild results; navigate-away results still cache (item-keyed). Caches cleared in enter_empty_state/rebuild_playlist/clear_session_state; rotate evicts per-item. 15 new unit tests + dev example image_text_probe (live-smoked: 1200x500 PNG, 4/4 lines in 29 ms; app T+Esc clean-exit smoke). DONE 2026-07-04: macOS Vision backend landed (subtask 2) and owner-smoked on the running app — text recognition + QR both confirmed working on Windows and macOS.

tasks.title: Light mode support for the HUD (appearance preference: System/Light/Dark)
tasks.description: The HUD rasterizer (pb-hud/src/hud.rs) currently hardcodes always-white text ([255,255,255]) with a black shadow/outline (tokens::TEXT/TEXT_DIM/SHADOW, hud.rs ~30-38) and a translucent-black panel background (tokens::BG) - there is no color/theme parameter threaded through render_table/render_centered/render_panel today, only background alpha is parameterized. Add a user-facing Appearance preference (System/Light/Dark, defaulting to System = current dark-on-black look unchanged) that flips the HUD to black text with a white shadow/halo and a light translucent panel background when resolved-light. Reuse the existing OS theme detection already used for the egui dialog window (winit's Window::theme() in pb-app/src/dialog.rs:404, dark_ui = window.theme() != Some(Theme::Light)) rather than hand-rolling a new registry/NSAppearance check - it already covers Windows (AppsUseLightTheme/DWM) and macOS (NSApp.effectiveAppearance) portably. Settings storage follows the existing ScaleModePref/StartupMode enum pattern in pb-app-core/src/settings.rs (Copy/Default/Serialize/Deserialize, #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")], #[default] variant, TOML-persisted, round-trip tested).

tasks.title: macOS: Cmd+W leaves the app in a dead state (window closed, Open/Open Folder do nothing)
tasks.description: Cmd+W closes the WindowGroup's only window (default SwiftUI behavior: app stays running, no applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed override in PhotoBlazeMacApp.swift). The app is then stuck: no visible window, and File > Open / Open Folder (and the application(_:open:) Finder-open delegate) don't bring a window back, because ContentView's .onAppear wiring (model.installMenuBarIfNeeded, openLaunchPathIfAny, openSettingsAction, the AppCore FFI bridge) never re-runs. Reopening from the Dock likely has the same problem (no applicationShouldHandleReopen override). Two candidate fixes: (1) mac-idiomatic — implement applicationShouldHandleReopen(hasVisibleWindows:) + make Open/Open Folder recreate the window if closed, matching apps like Preview/TextEdit; (2) simpler — override applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed to return true, so Cmd+W becomes equivalent to Esc (same RAM-teardown quit path already implemented and tested, see the no-trace-on-teardown work). Leaning toward (2): PhotoBlaze is explicitly a single-window app by design (no multi-window command anywhere), and (1) requires safely tearing down/recreating the AppCore FFI bridge + Metal canvas mid-process, an untested path in the same fragile window-lifecycle territory as the argv[1] windowless-launch bug already chased once (see PhotoBlazeMacApp.swift's launch-gotcha comment).
tasks.details: Files: mac/Sources/PhotoBlazeMac/PhotoBlazeMacApp.swift (AppDelegate, WindowGroup scene), CoreModel.swift (model.onAppear wiring, openLaunchPathIfAny). Owner decision needed on (1) vs (2) before implementing — see task description for the tradeoff. If (2) is chosen: add `func applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed(_ sender: NSApplication) -> Bool { true }` to AppDelegate and verify it routes through the same clean-teardown path as Esc (no disk writes, RAM caches dropped). If (1) is chosen: implement applicationShouldHandleReopen for the Dock-icon case, and make the Open/Open Folder menu commands + application(_:open:) recreate the WindowGroup scene when no window exists, re-running the .onAppear wiring exactly once.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual on the physical console (per owner-display-setup memory): launch PhotoBlaze, hit Cmd+W, then try File > Open, Open Folder, and clicking the Dock icon. Confirm the chosen behavior (app quits cleanly, or a window reliably reopens with menu/FFI wiring intact) with no leftover process or dead window state.

tasks.title: Folder nav (Cmd+Up/Left/Right): skip empty folders instead of "No supported images" dialog — IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-03
tasks.description:
Cmd+Left/Right (PrevFolder/NextFolder) and Cmd+Up (OpenParent) resolve purely by name-adjacency: open_sibling_cmd -> folder_tree::spawn_sibling/sibling_target does one read_dir on the parent and jumps to the immediately-adjacent folder name, with zero awareness of whether that folder actually contains photos. open_dir then opens it via pb_core::open::plan(LaunchInput::Directory(..)), which ALWAYS scans recursively (recursive: true, crates/pb-core/src/open.rs:86) -- so every Cmd+arrow hop triggers a full recursive walk (pb_app_core::scan::stream_scan) of the target subtree. Confirmed (owner repro): when that scan finishes having found zero images, crates/pb-mac-ffi/src/lib.rs:1291-1304 fires CoreEffect::ReportError("No supported images in that selection.") and the Mac host shows it as a Message dialog -- a hard stop that requires dismissing a dialog and re-pressing, instead of continuing to the next folder that does have photos.

Want: pressing Cmd+Right/Left/Up steps past an empty folder straight to the next/previous sibling (or ancestor) that actually has >=1 photo, with no dialog interruption for the common empty-intermediate-folder case -- reserve the dialog (or a toast) for the case where NO folder in that direction has any photos at all.

The risk (correctly flagged by the owner): since directory-open is always recursive, the existing full-subtree scan already doubles as an implicit 'does this folder have photos' check today -- but it's expensive machinery (spawns the Scanning progress dialog, rebuilds the playlist, enumerates the ENTIRE subtree with no early-exit-on-first-match) to run as a mere probe for every candidate folder in a skip loop. A folder with several consecutive empty siblings, each hiding a deep/huge nested tree (the exact ~/Library-shaped pathology scan.rs was hardened against before, see scan.rs:148-157), would make one keypress pay for N full recursive walks instead of one. The sibling-stepping path (folder_tree.rs spawn_sibling) also currently has NONE of the main scanner's cancellation plumbing -- it's a bare thread::spawn with no ScanProgress-style cancel flag, so a rapid re-press just orphans the previous probe thread (harmless today for one shallow read_dir; not fine for a multi-hop recursive search).
tasks.details: SETTLED DESIGN (owner + assistant, 2026-07-03): keyboard skips, clicks don't. (1) Scope: ⌘←/→ (PrevFolder/NextFolder) only — ⌘↑ can't hit this (parent opens recursively and the parent subtree ⊇ the current deck, so it can't scan empty while a photo is shown). (2) Skip = same-level siblings, stepping in the pressed direction past photo-less candidates via a dedicated early-exit recursive probe (a candidate counts as non-empty if ANY descendant has a supported image, matching the recursive open). (3) Terminal fallback on the keyboard path = a TOAST (not the modal): fires when nothing in that direction has photos (incl. plain end-of-row, today silent). The 'No supported images' modal stays for explicit opens (picker/drop/Finder/tree click) — clicks never redirect. (4) Probe hardening per prior scan.rs work: iterative walkdir, follow_links(false), error-tolerant, early-exit on first hit; hop cap AND an overall wall-clock budget (the expensive case is one huge photo-less subtree, which must be fully enumerated to conclude empty — a hop cap alone doesn't bound it); budget/cap exhaustion → toast. (5) Cancellation: TreeIo carries a cancel flag set on Drop, so a re-press SUPERSEDES the in-flight probe (no orphaned deep walks); checked per walk entry. (6) Stale-result guard: the Sibling result carries the origin root; tick drops it if the deck moved on. (7) Archives already correct for free: archive folder rows derive from image entry names, so photo-less archive folders can't exist — no skip needed there. Code surface: folder_tree.rs sibling_target/spawn_sibling (+TreeIo), scan.rs probe helper beside image_walker, app_core_impl.rs tick Sibling arm + open_sibling_cmd. OPTIONAL FOLLOW-UP (separate decision, not this task): tree-click on an empty folder still shows the modal because an empty scan never re-roots; re-rooting to an empty deck (nav-point, tree stays up) would honor the #47 promise better.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests (temp-dir fixtures, deterministic): probe finds a deep image / concludes empty / aborts on cancel + deadline; sibling search skips N empty siblings to the first non-empty one in each direction, exhausts to None at the row end, respects the hop cap (cap as a parameter so the test doesn't need 64 dirs) and a pre-set cancel flag; tick drops a Sibling result whose origin root no longer matches; a None result toasts. Manual: consecutive empty siblings (some with deep photo-less subtrees) hop straight to the next folder with photos, no dialog; rapid ⌘→ re-presses supersede cleanly (no thread pileup, no stall); all-empty direction toasts instead of dialog.

tasks.title: Evaluate Velopack: modern install UX + auto-updates for the Windows channel
tasks.description: Owner call (2026-07-03): 'auto updates are kinda non-optional in 2026.' Velopack (the maintained Squirrel successor, first-class Rust crate `velopack`) gives the Chrome/Discord install model — double-click, no wizard, installed + launched in seconds, per-user in %LocalAppData%, with built-in DELTA AUTO-UPDATES from a simple static feed (GitHub Releases works as the feed). This is an EVALUATION task, not a committed cutover: decide whether Velopack becomes the primary consumer channel (MSI kept for perMachine/enterprise), the beta channel only, or isn't a fit. Distinct from MSIX (still parked, ADR-018): Velopack is unpackaged Win32, so the registry integrations stay ordinary registry writes.
tasks.details: Questions the spike must answer: (1) Integration cost — the velopack crate wants a VelopackApp::build().run() hook at process start (fast-exit update hooks) in pb-app's main; measure its startup cost against the keypress→photon budget (should be ~0 when no update event, but MEASURE, per the prime directive). (2) File associations + the folder verb: Velopack installs per-user with a stable %LocalAppData% path — port the MSI's HKCR writes to HKCU\Software\Classes self-registration at install/update hook time (PhotoBlaze already has HKCU self-registration code from the 'Set default…' work, task #14.1) and confirm Open-with + Default-apps behave identically to the MSI install. (3) Update UX: silent background download + apply-on-restart (the viewer restarts in ms, so this fits) vs a toast offering restart-now; where the check runs (startup + daily?), and it must respect privacy #2 — an update CHECK is a network call, so it needs an off switch in Settings and must never phone home viewing data (it doesn't, but say so in the privacy notes). (4) Signing: vpk pack signs with signtool args — confirm Azure Trusted Signing /dlib flags pass through cleanly (same dlib/dmdf as release-windows.ps1). (5) Channel strategy: GitHub Releases as the update feed (vpk upload github), MSI + Velopack artifacts side by side on the same release; decide whether the MSI stays the website default. (6) Uninstall/upgrade coexistence: installing the Velopack build alongside an existing MSI install — define the migration story (likely: Velopack setup detects the MSI product and offers to remove it, or docs just say uninstall first). Output: a decisions.md ADR with the verdict + a working spike branch producing a signed Velopack setup.exe + one exercised delta update.
tasks.testStrategy: Spike acceptance: a signed PhotoBlaze Velopack setup.exe installs per-user with working file associations; publishing a second version to a test GitHub release delivers a delta update that applies on restart; startup overhead of the Velopack hook measured and recorded (target: unmeasurable against the 8.3 ms frame budget); the update check has a Settings off switch; ADR written with the channel decision.

tasks.title: Upstream the AES key-derivation cache to sevenz-rust2, then drop the vendored copy
tasks.description: PhotoBlaze vendors sevenz-rust2 0.21.1 (vendor/sevenz-rust2, wired via [patch.crates-io]) with one patch: encryption/aes.rs caches the derived AES key across blocks. Upstream re-derives the key (2^num_cycles_power SHA-256 rounds, ~10-40 ms at the standard cycles=19, scaling with password length) for EVERY block, and 7-Zip writes one salt per archive — so a non-solid stored+encrypted archive (one block per file) re-derives the identical key thousands of times. Measured: 3,000-file stored+encrypted archive with a 50-char password opened in 3.88 s vs 0.15 s for 7z t; with the cache, 0.08 s (48x). Owner's real 10 GB archive: 24 s -> ~4 s. 7-Zip itself caches the key the same way. STATUS: PR submitted AND MERGED (hasenbanck/sevenz-rust2#118, merged 2026-07-04). Remaining: wait for the next crates.io release (latest is still 0.21.2, pre-merge), then drop the vendored copy.
tasks.details: PR #118 is merged upstream — steps (1)-(3) are DONE. What remains is the teardown when a release ships (watch https://crates.io/crates/sevenz-rust2 or the repo's releases page for the first version after 0.21.2): (a) confirm the release actually contains the cache (check its CHANGELOG/diff — a patch release could ship without it); (b) bump the workspace dep to that version (crates/pb-source/Cargo.toml and the pb-app dev-dep), delete vendor/sevenz-rust2 and the [patch.crates-io] block in the root Cargo.toml (its comment documents this exact plan); (c) verify: cargo tree shows no path override, all pb-source tests pass (encrypted round-trip + wrong-password tests), and archive_probe on a many-file stored+encrypted long-password archive still opens fast (repro recipe: N small files, 7z a -mx0 -mhe=on -p<long password>; pre-cache baseline was 3.88 s / 3,000 files, cached 0.08 s). NOTE: upstream may have evolved the implementation during review (LRU instead of single-entry, std-feature gating) — the behavior contract to verify is 'derivation cost paid once per archive, wrong password still fails', not the exact patch shape.
tasks.testStrategy: PR accepted upstream (or an equivalent cache lands independently); after switching back to the crates.io release: cargo tree shows no path override for sevenz-rust2, vendor/ is gone, all pb-source tests pass (including the encrypted round-trip + wrong-password tests), and archive_probe on a 3,000-file stored+encrypted long-password archive still opens in well under 0.5 s.
